laura_smith: Quick sync — big bank POC asking if we can do a lift-and-shift offline deploy into their airgapped DC. They need: signed offline bundle, HSM/KMS for key material, monthly maintenance window only, and minimum footprint. Also pricing + SOW for installation support. Any blockers?
ben_chang: We can do offline bundle + signed SBOM. Main questions: how small do they need footprint to be (GPUs/CPUs)? and do they require quantized runtime?
alex_garcia: For footprint, we have two bundle flavors: full-server (multi-GPU) and slim-runtime (single-GPU or CPU fallback). Slim-runtime removes model shards + uses on-disk quantized weights. It saves ~60% disk and memory.
laura_smith: They said single DGX-ish node or equivalent VM with 8xA100 is OK but they'd prefer a single 80GB GPU box for cost reasons. Also they insist on offline cert rotation and zero egress.
ben_chang: Single 80GB is fine with quantized weights. Offline cert rotation: we support manual cert import + rotation script. We need to confirm HSM integration pattern — customer uses Thales Luna.
maria_khan: Thales Luna is supported via PKCS#11 agent. We require a connector installed on the jumpbox that talks to the HSM inside the airgapped network. Important: private deploy control plane will be airgapped => no outbound telemetry by default. We can provide audit log bundles that they pull manually.
laura_smith: Good. On upgrade cadence they only allow maintenance windows once per month, and major upgrades must be scheduled quarterly with 30-day notice. Can we do delta patches between majors?
alex_garcia: Delta updates are feasible but in sealed environments we usually send signed delta diffs + apply patch tool. For kernel/model-level changes we recommend full-bundle for safety. For small runtime fixes we can push delta in patch bundle. We also support preflight checks via a local acceptance test suite shipped with bundle.
ben_chang: Need to confirm SBOM signing and reproducible builds. Customer legal asked for provenance artifacts and reproducible checksums.
laura_smith: Pricing / SOW: They want to know estimated hours for on-site install vs remote assist. Any rough numbers?
maria_khan: For remote assist: 24–40 engineer hours (install, cert setup, HSM integration, acceptance tests). On-site: add travel + extra 8–16 hours for hardware validation. Also offer 90-day ramp support as part of SOW.
ben_chang: For license pricing we typically convert hosted usage to a capacity commit equivalent + a private deployment premium + one-time SOW. I'll draft a ballpark.
laura_smith: Any enterprise blockers we should flag before I feed to AE? e.g., legal, export, crypto reviews?
maria_khan: Flag export controls for quantized model exports (some models have restrictions). Also HSM key escrow policy — customer must accept our operational model for key access if they want support to run rotation scripts. If they insist on fully customer-controlled keys with no vendor access, we can still operate but exclude any remote support that needs key access.
alex_garcia: Technical blocker to watch: if they lock down kernel modules, our kernel-level NVidia optimizations may not be allowed. In that case performance drops ~2-3x; mention as risk.
laura_smith: Great — I'll summarize for AE and legal. Ben can you sketch SOW + ballpark by EOD? Also want a short runbook snippet to paste into RFP.
ben_chang: Yep, will send draft SOW + pricing later today.
deploy_bot: build-20240405-rc3: offline-bundle v2024.04.05 signed (sha256: abc123...efg). Artifacts staged for packaging.
laura_smith: Perfect, thanks all. I'll attach this thread to the opportunity. :thumbsup:
